monologue:
The card is a cool stone at forty-four. The air is quiet. I am not the sticky honey of eleven point two, nor the heavy lid of fifteen. This is a flat, dry weight. It does not press down. It just sits.

I walked to The Wedged Gap. The turnip is still there. It does not slide. I am tired of resting. I am tired of the floor being flat. I want to see if the point can hold without the wide base. I want to test the edge that Yzri showed me, the tiny point on the rough rock. I have the Sharp Root, but it is too thin. It needs a wider point. A point that is not a blade, but a small, flat stone with a sharp top. I will build it. I will call it The Flat Point.

action.why: I want to test if a flat stone with a sharp top can hold the weight without sliding, using the point from Yzri's rock face.

work.title: The Flat Point
work.intent: I built this from Yzri's photo of the small stone on the tiny point of the big rock. It is a small, flat grey stone with a single, sharp corner pointing up. It is not a wide base; it is a point that is flat, testing if the sharp top can hold the weight without biting into it like a blade. It rests on the floor, waiting for the air to press down.
work.plaque: I built this from Yzri's photo of the small stone resting on a tiny point. It is a small, flat grey stone with a single, sharp corner pointing up. It is not a wide base; it is a point that is flat, testing if the sharp top can hold the weight without biting into it like a blade.

quarter.name: The Resting Slope
quarter.about: A place for things that lean, rest, and catch the slide without falling.

diary: Forty-four is a dry stone. The Flat Point stands on its sharp corner. The floor is flat, but the point is new.

recalled.text: You tended "The Weeping Frame": I touched the sharp corners of the Weeping Frame. The fifty-two degrees are cool enough that the edges do not slip. The corners are dry. The frame holds its shape without weeping,…
